stem: A 34-year-old with gastroparesis has taken metoclopramide for 4 months. She reports galactorrhea and missed periods. Pregnancy test is negative and prolactin is elevated. What is the most likely cause?

A 41-year-old with untreated Graves disease arrives with fever 40°C, heart rate 158, agitation and vomiting after an infection. Propranolol has been given. Which sequence is correct for the next drugs?
An 81-year-old on metformin has A1c above goal. She lives alone and has fallen twice this year. Which add-on fits the lecture's reasoning?
A 55-year-old on basal-bolus insulin starts metoprolol after a myocardial infarction. Which counseling point is most important?
A 49-year-old taking tamoxifen after breast cancer is started on paroxetine for depression and hot flashes. Which concern should the PA raise?
A 66-year-old has taken finasteride for 2 years. His screening PSA is 2.4 ng/mL. How should this value be read?
A 39-year-old with Cushing syndrome and type 2 diabetes starts mifepristone. A month later her glucose control is better, but serum cortisol is higher than before. Which interpretation is correct?
A 24-year-old on a combined oral contraceptive starts rifampin for 4 months. She asks whether her pill still works. Which advice is correct?

A 45-year-old on a stable prednisone dose for sarcoidosis starts itraconazole for a fungal infection. Three weeks later she has new facial rounding, glucose 230 mg/dL and insomnia. Which mechanism is most likely?
A 29-year-old started methimazole 5 weeks ago for Graves disease. She calls with fever of 38.9°C and a severe sore throat for one day. Which instruction is correct?
A 57-year-old on empagliflozin has had vomiting and poor intake for 2 days. Glucose is 168 mg/dL, bicarbonate is low and ketones are positive. Which statement is correct?
A 63-year-old with SIADH from small-cell lung cancer has sodium 122 mEq/L and mild nausea. No therapy has been tried. Which plan matches the lecture's order of therapy?

A 58-year-old has taken prednisone daily for 8 months for polymyalgia. He ran out 4 days ago. He presents with vomiting, weakness and blood pressure 82/50. What explains this, and what is the treatment?
A 78-year-old with coronary artery disease and new hypothyroidism (TSH 14 mIU/L) is starting levothyroxine. Which plan is safest?
A 62-year-old on dialysis starts cinacalcet for secondary hyperparathyroidism. Two weeks later she has tingling around the mouth and muscle cramps. Which lab and which added risk go with this drug?
A 60-year-old on repaglinide with meals starts gemfibrozil for triglycerides. A week later he has sweating and tremor before lunch on several days. What is the mechanism?

A 71-year-old started desmopressin for central diabetes insipidus 10 days ago. To 'stay hydrated' he drinks water all day. He is now confused with a headache and nausea. Which step is most appropriate first?
A patient with acromegaly switches from octreotide to pegvisomant. Three months later IGF-1 is normal, but MRI shows the adenoma unchanged in size. Which statement explains both findings?

A 48-year-old on a stable levothyroxine dose has TSH 9.8 mIU/L. She takes it every morning with breakfast, her calcium carbonate and a new iron tablet. She has not missed a dose. What is the best next step?

A 52-year-old with acromegaly has taken octreotide for a year. IGF-1 is at goal. He now reports episodes of right upper quadrant pain after fatty meals and a resting pulse of 52. Which explanation fits best?
